page: Microsoft Azure M64dms_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine within the MDSMediumMemoryv2 family, virtualized on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system features 64 dedicated vCPUs powered by x86_64 Intel processors. The instance is designed for single-node vertical scalability, allocating dedicated host resources without GPU accelerators.

The core resource profile centers on high memory density, delivering 1792.0 GB of total RAM, which translates to 28.0 GB of memory per dedicated vCPU. Storage capabilities include a bundled 2199 GB local solid-state drive (SSD) for low-latency temporary data management, paired with support for Azure Premium Storage for persistent workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the platform consolidates large memory requirements into a single host footprint, reducing the operational complexity of distributed architectures. Tradeoffs include the absence of integrated GPUs and lack of complimentary public IPv4 addressing. The M64dms_v2 is structured primarily for large-scale enterprise databases, extensive in-memory caching systems, and demanding business intelligence or analytics pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure M64dms_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine within the MDSMediumMemoryv2 series, hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. Powered by x86_64 Intel processors, the instance delivers 64 dedicated vCPUs coupled with an expansive 1792.0 GB of system memory, providing 28.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It incorporates 2199 GB of bundled local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage configurations, though it omits hardware GPU acceleration and complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The hardware balance targets operational scenarios where primary bottlenecks stem from system memory capacity rather than parallel graphics processing. In qualitative terms, cost efficiency reflects its enterprise memory density, scaling expense against large-footprint single-node architectures rather than distributed clusters. The M64dms_v2 is engineered for memory-intensive workloads, including large-scale relational database management systems, in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning applications, and heavy in-memory data processing tasks.
